def calculate_dg(g_start, upper_bound=191):
    """
    Calculates the set D_g generated by starting with g_start,
    subject to the removal rules (i) and (ii) within {1, ..., upper_bound}.
    """
    S = set(range(1, upper_bound + 1))
    
    # Initialize the set of removed numbers R
    R = {g_start}
    
    # We use a loop that continues until no new numbers are added in an iteration
    while True:
        newly_added = set()
        
        # Rule (i): If x is removed, so is 2x
        for x in list(R):
            two_x = 2 * x
            if two_x <= upper_bound and two_x not in R:
                newly_added.add(two_x)
        
        # Rule (ii): If x and y are removed, then x + y is also removed
        # We only need to check pairs where at least one of the elements is newly added in this step
        # OR we check all pairs from the current set R (more robust for closure)
        
        # Check all pairs in the current set R
        current_R_list = list(R)
        for i in range(len(current_R_list)):
            x = current_R_list[i]
            for j in range(i, len(current_R_list)): # Start from i to include x+x
                y = current_R_list[j]
                sum_xy = x + y
                if sum_xy <= upper_bound and sum_xy not in R:
                    # Check if this sum was already marked for addition in this iteration
                    if sum_xy not in newly_added:
                        newly_added.add(sum_xy)

        # Update R and break if no additions occurred
        if not newly_added:
            break
        
        R.update(newly_added)
        
    # Calculate size and sum of the resulting set R
    size = len(R)
    total_sum = sum(R)
    
    return size, total_sum, R
